tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

scope.description: Required with items: "first_task", "continuation" or "new_task" (see the tool description). Omit on advance / done / start updates.

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: propose it and call this.

The result says which case below applies. When the box shows your question, it ends your turn: write no text after this call, since the recap and question say what the user needs and your work above holds the detail. Otherwise your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, with any question the box did not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label and message are the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead, an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence; the detail goes in message. No "@", no leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

message.description: For a reply: what the click sends, up to 300 characters of plain text — no "@" anywhere, no leading / or !. Omit when the label is the whole message.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, form_input, read_page). browser_batch cannot be nested. A tabs_create's new tabId is only returned when the batch ends — load that tab in a later call.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

Web search results for query: "Grand Canal Venice width metres 30 to 90 narrowest Rialto"

Links: [{"title":"Grand Canal (Venice)","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Canal_(Venice)"},{"title":"britannica.com","url":"https://www.britannica.com/print/article/502009"},{"title":"The Grand Canal in Venice, Italy","url":"https://veneziaautentica.com/?p=16072"},{"title":"The Grand Canal in Venice, Italy","url":"https://veneziaautentica.com/grand-canal-venice/"},{"title":"www.britannica.com","url":"https://www.britannica.com/print/article/241163"},{"title":"grand canal venice","url":"https://pickyourtrail.com/attractions/italy/grand-canal-venice"},{"title":"bridgeinfo.broer.no","url":"https://bridgeinfo.broer.no/bridge/index.php?ID=21"},{"title":"Rialto Bridge: Venice's Oldest Grand Canal Crossing","url":"https://geographyworlds.com/blog/rialto-bridge-venice/"},{"title":"bonjourvenise.fr","url":"https://bonjourvenise.fr/en/wp-json/wp/v2/posts/59"},{"title":"Venice…  one of the most interesting and lovely places in the world …","url":"https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/venice-animated/10867662"}]

The sources mostly agree that the Grand Canal is about 30 m wide at its narrowest, but they differ on the widest point.

- **Width range:** Wikipedia gives a range of 30 to 90 metres, and a travel guide gives the same range, noting it depends on the section. Britannica gives a narrower range, between 30 and 70 metres (100 and 225 feet). One French travel site gives a width of between 50 and 70 metres, which looks like an outlier.
- **Narrowest point and Rialto:** Britannica describes the Rialto Bridge as crossing over the narrowest point of the Grand Canal in the heart of Venice.
- **Rialto Bridge dimensions:** Sources disagree here too. Britannica puts the bridge's width at 20 metres (66 feet), while another bridge database lists it at 23 m.

Web search results for query: "Rialto Bridge span metres width arch single span 28 m"

Links: [{"title":"Rialto Bridge","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rialto_Bridge"},{"title":"Rialto Bridge","url":"https://www.britannica.com/topic/Rialto-Bridge"},{"title":"britannica.com","url":"https://www.britannica.com/print/article/502009"},{"title":"General Information","url":"https://structurae.net/en/structures/rialto-bridge"},{"title":"General Information","url":"https://structurae.net/en/structures/20000461"},{"title":"General Information","url":"https://structurae.net/structures/rialto-bridge"},{"title":"legend history and other curiosities about the rialto bridge in venice 386091","url":"https://www.immobiliare.it/news/en/living-in/venice/legend-history-and-other-curiosities-about-the-rialto-bridge-in-venice-386091/"},{"title":"meetingvenice.it","url":"https://meetingvenice.it/en/node/181"},{"title":"bridgeinfo.broer.no","url":"https://bridgeinfo.broer.no/bridge/index.php?ID=21"},{"title":"rialto bridge 272bb","url":"https://test.kureansiklopedi.com/en/detay/rialto-bridge-272bb"}]

The 28 m figure is supported, but sources disagree on the exact span and width.

- **Span:** Several sources give a figure near 28 m. Structurae lists the main span at 28.80 m, and Immobiliare.it describes a single 28-metre arch. Other sources differ: Wikipedia gives a longest span of 31.80 m, bridgeinfo.broer.no gives 29 m, and Britannica gives a lower chord of 25 m.
- **Width:** Wikipedia and Structurae put the deck width at 22.90 m. Meetingvenice.it gives 22 m, bridgeinfo.broer.no gives 23 m, and Britannica gives 20 m.
- **Design:** Britannica describes it as a single stone-arch span carrying a deck with two rows of shops. Structurae says the present stone bridge was designed by Antonio da Ponte and completed in 1591.

The variation likely reflects different measurement methods, such as chord versus arc length or deck width versus overall width. Structurae's 28.80 m main span is the most precise single figure I found.

# Research: the Venice map (`shared/map.ts`)

Scratch folder with every artefact named below: `/private/tmp/claude-502/-Users-makhlugjafarov-cognitex-Documents-regata-storica/69884729-7585-4b5d-ad26-4af5e194adaa/scratchpad/research/map/` (`map.txt`, `validate.mjs`, `gen.mjs`, `annotate.mjs`, `ts/shared/map.ts`, `ts/shared/map.test.ts`, `ts/src/sim/mapPhysics.ts`, `ts/src/render/mapGeometry.ts`, `prove_apis.mjs`, `prove_rotation.mjs`). Nothing in the repo was touched.

## 1. The problem, in the words of the spec

SPEC.md section 7: "One compact, invented district that reads as Venice at a glance: about 400 m x 300 m, crossable in roughly 40 s at full speed." It needs a **main canal** ("a wide S-shaped canal, Canal Grande style, about 30 m wide, cutting across the map. The open fighting lane"), **side canals** ("a grid of about 8 narrow canals, 8 to 10 m wide, with tight bends and a few dead ends. One gondola fits easily, two scrape. Ambush territory"), a **lagoon basin** ("open water along one edge. Big open fights, and the densest cluster of crates, so it pulls teams into fights"), **bridges** ("6 to 8 arched stone bridges plus one large covered bridge at the centre as the main landmark, Rialto style. Boats pass under every bridge"), a **bell tower** ("tall enough to be seen from every viewport, for orientation") and **obstacles** ("wooden pile clusters in the lagoon").

"How the map is built. The whole map is one ASCII grid in shared/map.ts, 8 m per cell, about 50 x 38 cells. Physics builds its walls from the grid, and the renderer builds the buildings from the same grid." Legend: `B` building, `~` water, `=` bridge over water (visual only), `L` lagoon, `S` spawn dock, `C` crate point, `T` landmark tower. "Coordinates: metres, Y up, water surface at y = 0, map origin at the centre. The 2D physics uses (x, z) of the 3D world."

Rules from elsewhere in the spec that the map must serve: respawn "at a random dock ... at least 80 m from every enemy boat (about 16 docks around the map)" (section 5); "Wooden crates float at about 24 fixed points" (section 6); the minimap "shows an enemy only for 2 s after it fires, or while it is in the open lagoon" (section 7); top speed 10 m/s, 16 m/s with Boost (section 8); `shared/map.ts` is a contract file, "written together in the base phase, then read-only for every agent" (section 11).

## 2. Decisions, why, and what was rejected

| Decision | Why | Rejected |
|---|---|---|
| **Grid 50 x 38, 8 m cells = 400 x 304 m.** The border is one ring of `B`. | Exactly the spec's size. The border ring gives the physics a closed box for free. | A separate "world bounds" collider: one more thing to keep in step with the grid. |
| **Legend extended with `R` (covered bridge, water for physics) and `P` (pile cluster, solid circle).** | The spec asks for a Rialto-style covered bridge and pile clusters but has no chars for them. `R` as a 2 x 4 block gives the renderer a roofed deck 16 m deep spanning the full 32 m canal; `P` is a 2.5 m-radius ball so boats slip around it. | Encoding the Rialto as `=` cells: the renderer could not tell it apart. A full solid `P` cell (8 x 8 m) is a block, not a cluster of poles. |
| **Main canal 4 cells (32 m) wide on the straights, a reversed S like the real Canal Grande:** west mouth (rows 6-9) east to col 29, a 45-degree run south-west to a hairpin at col 13, then east (rows 23-26) under the covered bridge into the bacino. | "About 30 m" and the real canal is 30-90 m wide (Wikipedia). The 45-degree run is painted 5 cells tall per column: every cell of it is inside a 3 x 3 all-water window, so the perpendicular width never drops below 24 m (5/sqrt 2 = 3.5 cells = 28 m). The hairpin gives the long lane two blind corners. | 90-degree stair bends: the inside corner cuts to 24 m and reads as a staircase. A main canal running north-south: with the lagoon on one side the long sides of the map should carry the lane. |
| **Lagoon along the east edge: a 7-cell strip (56 m) for the full height plus a 5 x 15 bacino bulge in front of the canal mouth** (307 `L` cells, 328 with the markers on it). | "Open water along one edge". The bulge is where the Canal Grande meets the bacino in Venice; 12 cells (96 m) of open water at the mouth is where the big fights go. The border column behind it is still `B` (physics) but `lagoonEdge: 'east'` tells the renderer to draw it as a breakwater, not houses. | A lagoon along the south edge under the hairpin: it would make the quiet SW quarter the hot zone and put the covered bridge next to open water. |
| **Eight side-canal networks, 215 cells (1.7 km), 31 tight bends, 19 mouths, 3 dead ends.** All 1 cell (8 m) wide: a 6 m x 1.4 m gondola "fits easily, two scrape". | Each rio links two different thick-water places (so hunters can loop, nobody is forced to turn around in 8 m), except three spurs that end in a pocket with a crate or a quiet dock. | 2-cell rii (16 m): two boats pass, the ambush feel is gone; the validator refuses any 2-wide water outside the main canal and lagoon. More than 4 dead ends: boats respawning or fleeing into them get cornered too often. |
| **Covered bridge `R` at cols 26-27, rows 23-26** (centre x = 16 m, z = 48 m, 51 m from the origin): deck north-south, span 32 m, depth 16 m. **Tower `T` at (19, 22)** (x = -44 m, z = 28 m), on the tip of the wedge between the diagonal and the lower arm, water on three sides. | Both central; both on the lower arm so a boat coming out of the hairpin sees the tower and then passes under the Rialto. The real Rialto spans about 28.8 m and is about 22.9 m wide (Structurae), so 32 x 16 m at 8 m resolution reads right. | Tower inside a block: it would be visible but no boat could pass it closely. |
| **16 docks** (4 / 4 / 3 / 5 per quadrant), never adjacent, each beside a `B` quay, heading derived (section 3.3). | Monte Carlo (4000 random 5-enemy layouts) shows 100 % always have a dock 80 m or more from every enemy, 7.3 candidates on average; the farthest water cell from any dock is 96 m. | Docks only along the main canal: the respawn rule then fails whenever a fight sits mid-canal. |
| **24 crates: 12 in the lagoon (7 of them in one 40 m cluster in the bacino), 6 on the main canal, 6 in the rii and dead-end pockets.** | Lagoon density 3.66 per 100 cells vs 2.47 elsewhere, and the biggest cluster is in the bacino: the pull the spec wants. Every crate is at most 136 m of water from the nearest dock. | Equal spread: nothing pulls teams into the open. |
| **Walls = greedy rectangle merge of `B` and `T` cells** (69 rectangles for 1082 solid cells, 15.7 cells each); `P` = ball colliders. | 69 cuboids instead of 1082 keeps the broad phase trivial and gives the renderer 69 blocks to decorate. Merging `T` into a block is correct for physics; the tower position is exported separately for the renderer. | Per-cell colliders: 1082 cuboids and visible "seams" in the bounce. A trimesh from the water outline: more code, and Rapier trimeshes are hollow, boats inside would not be pushed out. |
| **Coordinates: origin at the centre, row 0 at negative z (north, the far side), col 0 at negative x (west). Heading = Rapier rotation angle, 0 = +x, +PI/2 = +z.** | One rule for everybody: Rapier's (x, y) is the world's (x, z), so `body.rotation()` is the heading and `mesh.rotation.y = -heading` (three.js `makeRotationY` maps +x to (cos, 0, -sin), proved in `prove_apis.mjs`). | Row 0 at positive z: then the text on screen is upside down compared to the top-down minimap. |
| **Parsing throws `MapError` at import time for structural breakage** (ragged lines, unknown chars, border, water in more than one region, missing tower/lagoon/R, a dock without a quay, a pile not in water); **the design checks live in `shared/map.test.ts`** (vitest). | A broken edit by any track fails `npm run dev` and `npm test` within a second. The heavy checks (diameter, density, Monte Carlo) cost about 100 ms, too much for import. | Only a test: a bad merge would reach the demo PC. |

### Measured numbers (from `validate.mjs`, section 5 has the full output)

- Water 814 cells (43 %): main canal 275 cells (81 % of it inside a 4 x 4 water window; 24 m minimum by construction), rii 215 cells = 1720 m, lagoon 307 `L` (mask 328).
- Side canal networks 8 (lengths 24, 30, 95, 20, 11, 8, 19, 8 cells); bends 31; mouths 19; dead ends 3 at (15,1), (14,14), (8,22).
- Bridges: 7 arches (3 over the main canal at cols 9, 20 and 35; 4 over rii) + 1 covered. Tower 52 m from the centre.
- Docks 16, crates 24 (12 in the lagoon), piles 4.
- Longest shortest water path (network diameter): 77 cells = 616 m = 62 s at 10 m/s, between the west mouth (1,6) and the lagoon's far corner (48,36). That is exactly the Manhattan distance between the grid's opposite corners (47 + 30), so no shorter network is possible without shrinking the map. The main canal itself is 64 cells (512 m, 51 s) from west mouth to lagoon mouth; the quickest west-to-lagoon crossing uses the N2 rio: 45 cells = 360 m = 36 s, which is the spec's "roughly 40 s".
- Wall rectangles 69, plus 4 pile circles.

## 3. The map, the parser and the algorithms

### 3.1 The map (`map.txt`, 38 lines of 50 chars; the same text sits in `MAP_TEXT` in `shared/map.ts`)

```text
<<MAP>>
```

Annotated rendering (column ruler on top and bottom, row numbers both sides; the second block shows `B` as `#`, canal water as space, lagoon as `.`):

```text

```

**Reading it as a district.** The Canal Grande enters at the west (rows 6-9, under two arches at cols 9 and 20), bends south at col 29 past the bend dock (29,10), runs 45 degrees south-west past the dock at (23,13) and the crate at (26,12), reaches the hairpin at col 13-15 (the quietest part of the lane, with the dock (15,26)) and heads east along rows 23-26, past the campanile at (19,22), under the covered bridge (cols 26-27) and the arch at col 35, into the bacino (cols 37-41, rows 17-31) and the lagoon strip.

Named rii (all 8 m wide; the names are only for the design notes):

| Network | Cells | Route | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| N1 Rio Nord | (7,5)-(7,3)-(24,3)-(24,5), spur (15,2)-(15,1) | loop north of the upper arm, two mouths into it, arch at (11,3), dock (20,3), crate in the dead end (15,1) | a bypass: overtake or ambush anyone fighting in the upper arm |

| S2 Rio dei Tolentini | (22,27)-(22,30)-(26,30)-(26,31)-(36,31) | lower arm to the bacino, arch (31,31) | ambush exit onto the bacino crate cluster |

**Fight flow.** The lagoon holds half the crates (12, with 7 within 40 m of each other in the bacino), so every life starts with a run to the open water; the bacino is where 4 to 6 boats meet with nowhere to hide and where the minimap shows everyone. The lower arm (rows 23-26) is the second lane: it feeds the bacino through its mouth, through S2, S3 and E2, so a team leaving the lagoon has four exits to choose and four doors to watch. The upper arm is the sniper lane (240 m straight, two arches to duck behind); N1 above it is the counter: a boat in N1 pops out of either mouth behind a boat camping the arm. The diagonal with the tower is the connecting hall; W1, W2 and E1 are the ambush rii across it, each with a bend that hides the boat until the last 16 m. Dead ends are deliberate traps: a pocket with a crate at (15,1) and (14,14) and the quiet dock spur at (8,22). The far west and south (W3/S1/S4) is where the respawn rule puts boats when the fight is in the east: 4 docks there are 160 m or more from the bacino.

### 3.2 Parser: `shared/map.ts` (typechecks under the repo's tsconfig with `noUnusedLocals`/`noUnusedParameters` added)

```ts
<<MAP_TS>>
```

### 3.3 Algorithms in words

**Coordinates.** `x = (col - W/2 + 0.5) * 8`, `z = (row - H/2 + 0.5) * 8`; the inverse is `col = floor(x / 8 + W/2)`, `row = floor(z / 8 + H/2)`, clamped. Cell (0,0) is centred at (-196, -148), cell (49,37) at (196, 148). Y is up, the water is y = 0, row 0 is north = negative z (the far side of the default camera). A boat's cell is taken from its centre; a 6 m boat is always within one cell of its centre cell.

**Heading convention.** `heading` is the Rapier 2D rotation angle: forward = (cos h, sin h) in (x, z), so 0 = east, +PI/2 = south, PI = west, -PI/2 = north. Proof: a collider placed 1 m along the body's local +x ends up at (cos 0.7, sin 0.7) after `RigidBodyDesc.fixed().setRotation(0.7)` (`prove_rotation.mjs`). For three.js, `mesh.rotation.y = -heading` (`makeRotationY(t)` sends +x to (cos t, 0, -sin t), `prove_apis.mjs`).

**Dock heading (face away from the quay into open water).**
1. `v = sum over B/T 4-neighbours of (dock - neighbour)`: a vector pointing away from the quays. A dock with the quay to its south gets v = (0, -1) = north.
2. Among the navigable 4-neighbours pick the direction with the largest `dot(dir, v)`.
3. Ties, including v = 0 (a dock in a 1-wide rio with quays on both sides), go to the direction with the most water ahead (count up to 3 cells), then to the fixed order E, W, S, N. Example: dock (7,16) in W1 has quays north and south, water 2 cells to the west and 1 to the east, so it faces west (180 degrees). Result for all 16 docks: `(20,3) 0, (14,6) 90, (42,6) 0, (29,10) 180, (38,12) 0, (23,13) 0, (7,16) 180, (37,17) 0, (8,22) 180, (36,23) 90, (15,26) -90, (30,26) -90, (38,31) -90, (10,33) 0, (26,33) 0, (42,35) 0` degrees. The test checks the cell one step along the heading is never a building.

**Lagoon mask (minimap reveal).** Flood fill from every `L` through `L`, `C`, `S`, `P`. Crates and docks that sit on lagoon water are lagoon cells (the crate at (43,21) is `C` in the text but `isLagoon` is true there); a dock at the canal mouth such as (36,23), adjacent to the bacino, counts as lagoon too, which is right for a spawn with 3 s of protection. `isLagoon(x, z)` is one array read.

**Greedy wall merge.** Scan row-major; at the first unused `B`/`T` cell extend right while cells are solid and unused (width w), then extend down while the whole w-wide strip is solid and unused (height h); mark the rectangle used; emit centre + full size in metres. It is not the minimum rectangle cover but it covers every solid cell exactly once (the test sums the areas: 1082 cells) and yields 69 rectangles, the largest 24 x 168 m (the west border strip) and 400 x 8 m (the north border). Rapier wants half extents: `ColliderDesc.cuboid(w / 2, d / 2).setTranslation(x, z)` (verified in the installed `rapier.d.ts`: `cuboid(hx, hy)`, "half-width along its local x/y axis").

**Bridges.** Connected components of `=` and of `R`. A component must be a filled rectangle. The deck axis is the one with `B` at both ends (for a 1-cell arch over a rio that is unambiguous; a 1 x 4 column over the main canal has `B` above and below). `length` = span across the water in metres, `width` = depth along the canal. The renderer puts the deck 4 m above the water so a gondola with its bow lantern passes under.

**Width classes (validator and test).** `thick` = inside a 3 x 3 all-water window, `wide2` = inside a 2 x 2 window, `thin` = not inside any 2 x 2 window. Main canal = thick cells outside the lagoon mask, plus 2 x 2-covered cells touching it (the rounded hairpin tip). Side canals = thin cells. Any other water (2-wide blobs) is a design error and fails the check. Dead end = thin cell with exactly one navigable neighbour. Bend = thin cell with two perpendicular navigable neighbours.

**Distances.** Breadth-first search over 4-connected water, 8 m per step; the diameter is the maximum over all 814 sources (814 x 814 is instant). Monte Carlo for the respawn rule: 4000 layouts of 5 enemies on random water cells, count docks 80 m or more from all five (Euclidean, cell centres).

| A line in `MAP_TEXT` is shorter or longer (a dropped char in a merge) | `parseMap` throws `MapError: row r has n chars, expected 50` at import time; `npm run dev` fails to load the scene and `npm test` fails. |

| A `B` painted in the border breaks it, or a water cell on the border | Border must be all `B`; a water cell on the border would let a boat leave the world. Throws. |
| Two water regions (an edit seals a rio) | Flood fill from one water cell must reach all 814; throws naming the first cut-off cell. A crate or dock in a sealed region would be unreachable otherwise. |
| A dock with no `B` neighbour (floating in the canal) | Throws: no quay, no heading. A dock next to a `T` counts the tower as a quay for the heading but still needs a `B` neighbour (the design rule). |

| Dock in a 1-wide rio with quays both sides (`v = 0`) | Tie-break by water ahead, then E, W, S, N; it always faces along the rio. |

| Two docks adjacent, a crate next to a dock | Not a parse error (the sim could tolerate it) but a design error: the test asserts Chebyshev distance >= 2 between docks; the validator also checks crates vs docks and crates vs crates. |
| Respawn rule finds no dock 80 m from every enemy | Possible only in adversarial layouts (Monte Carlo found none in 4000 random ones, minimum 1 candidate). `respawnCandidates` falls back to the single farthest dock so the sim never stalls. |
| Boat centre exactly on a cell edge (x = -0.1 vs 3.9) | `floor` puts -0.1 in col 24 and 3.9 in col 25; the test pins both. |

| Bridge touching another bridge | They would merge into one component and fail the rectangle/abutment rule; keep one cell of water between them. |
| `R` deeper than 3 cells or narrower than the canal | Design check: depth 2..3, span 3..5, every `R` cell inside the main canal, centre within 80 m of the origin. |
| A `P` touching a building or outside the lagoon | Throws at parse (surrounded by water) and the test checks the lagoon mask; two adjacent `P` fail the validator. |
| `T` painted on water, or two towers | Exactly one `T`; the generator refuses to paint `T` on water; a `T` that touches no `B` is flagged by the validator (a tower needs a block). |

| Crates respawn with drift ("light bodies that drift") | Crate spawn points are cells; the sim respawns at the cell centre and may clamp the body back into the cell when it drifts more than 4 m, so a crate cannot drift under a bridge abutment. |
| Map size other than 50 x 38 (an alternative map for a rematch) | `parseMap` is size-agnostic (>= 8 x 8); all helpers read `map.width/height/cell`; only the test pins 50 x 38 for this district. |

## 1. The problem, in the words of the spec

SPEC.md section 7: "One compact, invented district that reads as Venice at a glance: about 400 m x 300 m, crossable in roughly 40 s at full speed." It needs a **main canal** ("a wide S-shaped canal, Canal Grande style, about 30 m wide, cutting across the map. The open fighting lane"), **side canals** ("a grid of about 8 narrow canals, 8 to 10 m wide, with tight bends and a few dead ends. One gondola fits easily, two scrape. Ambush territory"), a **lagoon basin** ("open water along one edge. Big open fights, and the densest cluster of crates, so it pulls teams into fights"), **bridges** ("6 to 8 arched stone bridges plus one large covered bridge at the centre as the main landmark, Rialto style. Boats pass under every bridge"), a **bell tower** ("tall enough to be seen from every viewport, for orientation") and **obstacles** ("wooden pile clusters in the lagoon").

"How the map is built. The whole map is one ASCII grid in shared/map.ts, 8 m per cell, about 50 x 38 cells. Physics builds its walls from the grid, and the renderer builds the buildings from the same grid." Legend: `B` building, `~` water, `=` bridge over water (visual only), `L` lagoon, `S` spawn dock, `C` crate point, `T` landmark tower. "Coordinates: metres, Y up, water surface at y = 0, map origin at the centre. The 2D physics uses (x, z) of the 3D world."

Rules from elsewhere in the spec that the map must serve: respawn "at a random dock ... at least 80 m from every enemy boat (about 16 docks around the map)" (section 5); "Wooden crates float at about 24 fixed points" (section 6); the minimap "shows an enemy only for 2 s after it fires, or while it is in the open lagoon" (section 7); top speed 10 m/s, 16 m/s with Boost (section 8); `shared/map.ts` is a contract file, "written together in the base phase, then read-only for every agent" (section 11).

### 3.3 Algorithms in words

**Coordinates.** `x = (col - W/2 + 0.5) * 8`, `z = (row - H/2 + 0.5) * 8`; the inverse is `col = floor(x / 8 + W/2)`, `row = floor(z / 8 + H/2)`, clamped. Cell (0,0) is centred at (-196, -148), cell (49,37) at (196, 148). Y is up, the water is y = 0, row 0 is north = negative z (the far side of the default camera). A boat's cell is taken from its centre; a 6 m boat is always within one cell of its centre cell.

**Heading convention.** `heading` is the Rapier 2D rotation angle: forward = (cos h, sin h) in (x, z), so 0 = east, +PI/2 = south, PI = west, -PI/2 = north. Proof: a collider placed 1 m along the body's local +x ends up at (cos 0.7, sin 0.7) after `RigidBodyDesc.fixed().setRotation(0.7)` (`prove_rotation.mjs`). For three.js, `mesh.rotation.y = -heading` (`makeRotationY(t)` sends +x to (cos t, 0, -sin t), `prove_apis.mjs`).

**Dock heading (face away from the quay into open water).**
1. `v = sum over B/T 4-neighbours of (dock - neighbour)`: a vector pointing away from the quays. A dock with the quay to its south gets v = (0, -1) = north.
2. Among the navigable 4-neighbours pick the direction with the largest `dot(dir, v)`.
3. Ties, including v = 0 (a dock in a 1-wide rio with quays on both sides), go to the direction with the most water ahead (count up to 3 cells), then to the fixed order E, W, S, N. Example: dock (7,16) in W1 has quays north and south, water 2 cells to the west and 1 to the east, so it faces west (180 degrees). Result for all 16 docks: `(20,3) 0, (14,6) 90, (42,6) 0, (29,10) 180, (38,12) 0, (23,13) 0, (7,16) 180, (37,17) 0, (8,22) 180, (36,23) 90, (15,26) -90, (30,26) -90, (38,31) -90, (10,33) 0, (26,33) 0, (42,35) 0` degrees. The test checks the cell one step along the heading is never a building.

**Lagoon mask (minimap reveal).** Flood fill from every `L` through `L`, `C`, `S`, `P`. Crates and docks that sit on lagoon water are lagoon cells (the crate at (43,21) is `C` in the text but `isLagoon` is true there); a dock at the canal mouth such as (36,23), adjacent to the bacino, counts as lagoon too, which is right for a spawn with 3 s of protection. `isLagoon(x, z)` is one array read.

**Greedy wall merge.** Scan row-major; at the first unused `B`/`T` cell extend right while cells are solid and unused (width w), then extend down while the whole w-wide strip is solid and unused (height h); mark the rectangle used; emit centre + full size in metres. It is not the minimum rectangle cover but it covers every solid cell exactly once (the test sums the areas: 1082 cells) and yields 69 rectangles, the largest 24 x 168 m (the west border strip) and 400 x 8 m (the north border). Rapier wants half extents: `ColliderDesc.cuboid(w / 2, d / 2).setTranslation(x, z)` (verified in the installed `rapier.d.ts`: `cuboid(hx, hy)`, "half-width along its local x/y axis").

**Bridges.** Connected components of `=` and of `R`. A component must be a filled rectangle. The deck axis is the one with `B` at both ends (for a 1-cell arch over a rio that is unambiguous; a 1 x 4 column over the main canal has `B` above and below). `length` = span across the water in metres, `width` = depth along the canal. The renderer puts the deck 4 m above the water so a gondola with its bow lantern passes under.

**Width classes (validator and test).** `thick` = inside a 3 x 3 all-water window, `wide2` = inside a 2 x 2 window, `thin` = not inside any 2 x 2 window. Main canal = thick cells outside the lagoon mask, plus 2 x 2-covered cells touching it (the rounded hairpin tip). Side canals = thin cells. Any other water (2-wide blobs) is a design error and fails the check. Dead end = thin cell with exactly one navigable neighbour. Bend = thin cell with two perpendicular navigable neighbours.

**Distances.** Breadth-first search over 4-connected water, 8 m per step; the diameter is the maximum over all 814 sources (814 x 814 is instant). Monte Carlo for the respawn rule: 4000 layouts of 5 enemies on random water cells, count docks 80 m or more from all five (Euclidean, cell centres).

## 4. Edge cases and how they are handled

| Case | Handling |
|---|---|
| A line in `MAP_TEXT` is shorter or longer (a dropped char in a merge) | `parseMap` throws `MapError: row r has n chars, expected 50` at import time; `npm run dev` fails to load the scene and `npm test` fails. |
| Unknown char (tab, `O` for `0`, Windows `\r`) | `\r` is stripped and trailing spaces trimmed; any other char throws with row/col. |
| Comment lines and blank lines inside the literal | Lines starting with `#` and empty lines are skipped, so the legend can stay in the text. |
| A `B` painted in the border breaks it, or a water cell on the border | Border must be all `B`; a water cell on the border would let a boat leave the world. Throws. |
| Two water regions (an edit seals a rio) | Flood fill from one water cell must reach all 814; throws naming the first cut-off cell. A crate or dock in a sealed region would be unreachable otherwise. |
| A dock with no `B` neighbour (floating in the canal) | Throws: no quay, no heading. A dock next to a `T` counts the tower as a quay for the heading but still needs a `B` neighbour (the design rule). |
| A dock sealed on all sides | `dockHeading` throws before that (no navigable neighbour). |
| Dock in a 1-wide rio with quays both sides (`v = 0`) | Tie-break by water ahead, then E, W, S, N; it always faces along the rio. |
| Dock at a dead end (8,22) | Quays on three sides; `v` points out of the pocket, so the boat spawns facing the exit, reverse never needed. |
| Two docks adjacent, a crate next to a dock | Not a parse error (the sim could tolerate it) but a design error: the test asserts Chebyshev distance >= 2 between docks; the validator also checks crates vs docks and crates vs crates. |
| Respawn rule finds no dock 80 m from every enemy | Possible only in adversarial layouts (Monte Carlo found none in 4000 random ones, minimum 1 candidate). `respawnCandidates` falls back to the single farthest dock so the sim never stalls. |
| Boat centre exactly on a cell edge (x = -0.1 vs 3.9) | `floor` puts -0.1 in col 24 and 3.9 in col 25; the test pins both. |
| Position outside the grid (a physics explosion) | `colOf`/`rowOf` clamp; `cellAt` returns `B`; `isLagoon` false; the sim should also clamp the body, the border colliders normally prevent it. |
| Crate or dock on lagoon water is `C`/`S` in the text, not `L` | The lagoon mask floods through `C`, `S`, `P`, so `isLagoon` is still true there. A crate at a rio mouth touching the bacino counts as lagoon: acceptable (it is in the open). |
| Bridge `=` over the main canal must span the full width | Each column of a bridge component needs `B` at both ends; a 3-cell bridge over a 4-cell canal fails ("abutment missing"). |
| Bridge touching another bridge | They would merge into one component and fail the rectangle/abutment rule; keep one cell of water between them. |
| `R` deeper than 3 cells or narrower than the canal | Design check: depth 2..3, span 3..5, every `R` cell inside the main canal, centre within 80 m of the origin. |
| A `P` touching a building or outside the lagoon | Throws at parse (surrounded by water) and the test checks the lagoon mask; two adjacent `P` fail the validator. |
| `T` painted on water, or two towers | Exactly one `T`; the generator refuses to paint `T` on water; a `T` that touches no `B` is flagged by the validator (a tower needs a block). |
| The renderer draws the east border as a wall of houses behind the lagoon | `lagoonEdge: 'east'`: the track C code draws that border column as a breakwater/diga and extends the water plane beyond it; physics keeps the `B` ring. |
| Boats in the 45-degree run see "stair" walls | Each step is 8 m; at 10 m/s that is 0.8 s per step, the same cadence as the real canal's facades. The renderer may chamfer the steps (a diagonal facade per step cell) without touching the physics rectangles. |
| 2-wide water sneaks in (a rio drawn next to another) | Validator and test: every water cell outside lagoon/main must be thin; the rounded hairpin tip is the only allowed 2 x 2 island because it touches the thick canal. |
| Side-canal count changes when a link is added (components merge) | Expected: W3+S1+S4 are one 95-cell network by design; the test allows 6..12 networks and checks length, bends and dead ends instead of an exact count. |
| Crates respawn with drift ("light bodies that drift") | Crate spawn points are cells; the sim respawns at the cell centre and may clamp the body back into the cell when it drifts more than 4 m, so a crate cannot drift under a bridge abutment. |
| Map size other than 50 x 38 (an alternative map for a rematch) | `parseMap` is size-agnostic (>= 8 x 8); all helpers read `map.width/height/cell`; only the test pins 50 x 38 for this district. |

input.summary: Designed a 50 x 38 cell (400 x 304 m, 8 m cells) Venice district that satisfies SPEC.md section 7 and the respawn/crate/minimap rules, and proved it with an executable validator. The main canal is a reversed S like the Canal Grande: 4 cells (32 m) wide on the straights, a 45-degree run painted 5 cells tall so every cell is inside a 3x3 water window (24 m minimum), entering at the west edge, hairpin at col 13, exiting east under a 2x4 covered bridge (new legend char R, water for physics) into a 7-cell lagoon strip plus a 5x15 bacino bulge (new legend char P for pile clusters as 2.5 m balls). Eight 1-wide side-canal networks (215 cells, 1.7 km, 31 tight bends, 19 mouths, 3 dead ends), 7 arch bridges (3 over the main canal) + 1 covered, tower 52 m from the centre on a water-edge wedge, 16 docks (every quadrant, never adjacent, each with a quay; Monte Carlo 100% of 4000 random 5-enemy layouts leave a dock >= 80 m away, mean 7.3 candidates), 24 crates (12 in the lagoon, densest 40 m cluster of 7 in the bacino, farthest crate 136 m by water from a dock). Network diameter 77 cells = 616 m (62 s at 10 m/s), which equals the Manhattan distance of the grid's opposite corners, so it cannot be shorter; the quickest west-to-lagoon crossing is 360 m = 36 s via rio N2 (the spec's "roughly 40 s"). Deliverables in the scratch folder: map.txt (38 lines of 50 chars), validate.mjs (standalone, prints ALL CHECKS PASSED), gen.mjs (painter), annotate.mjs, final.md (94 KB, with the map, annotated rendering, validator output, decisions, algorithms, edge cases, day-one tests, sources), and TypeScript ready to paste: ts/shared/map.ts (parser: Legend type, parseMap -> {width,height,cells,navigable,lagoon,lagoonEdge,lagoonCells,walls(greedy merged rects, 69 for 1082 solid cells),docks{x,z,heading},crates,bridges{x,z,orientation,length,width,kind},tower,piles}, cellAt/colOf/rowOf/cellCentre/isLagoon/isNavigable, MAP_TEXT, MAP), ts/shared/map.test.ts (vitest, 12 tests pass in 205 ms), ts/src/sim/mapPhysics.ts (Rapier cuboid/ball colliders, respawnCandidates) and ts/src/render/mapGeometry.ts (instanced placeholder district). All four TS files typecheck with the repo's exact tsconfig options plus noUnusedLocals/noUnusedParameters. Coordinates: origin at the centre, x = (col - W/2 + 0.5)*8, z = (row - H/2 + 0.5)*8, Y up, row 0 = north = negative z; heading = Rapier rotation angle (0 = +x, +PI/2 = +z), mesh.rotation.y = -heading, both proved by running the installed Rapier 0.21.0 and three 0.186.1. No file in the repo was created or modified.

decisions.decision: Grid 50 x 38 cells at 8 m with a full B border ring; parser is size-agnostic (>= 8 x 8)
decisions.rationale: Exactly the spec's 'about 50 x 38, 400 x 300 m'; the border ring is the physics box for free
decisions.alternatives: A separate world-bounds collider kept in step with the grid by hand

decisions.decision: Extend the legend with R (covered bridge, 2 cells deep x 4 across, water for physics) and P (pile cluster, solid ball of radius 2.5 m)
decisions.rationale: The spec needs a Rialto-style landmark and lagoon piles but gives no chars; R lets the renderer roof it, P is a cluster boats can slip around
decisions.alternatives: Encode the Rialto as '=' (renderer cannot tell it apart); a full 8 x 8 m solid P cell (a block, not poles)

decisions.decision: Main canal as a reversed S: west mouth rows 6-9, bend at col 29, 45-degree run painted 5 cells tall per column, hairpin at col 13, lower arm rows 23-26 into the bacino
decisions.rationale: 32 m on the straights, never under 24 m on the diagonal (every cell inside a 3x3 water window); the real Canal Grande is 30-90 m and is itself a reversed S; two blind corners on the lane
decisions.alternatives: 90-degree stair bends (inside corner cuts to 24 m, reads as stairs); a north-south lane (the lagoon side would then be short)

decisions.decision: Lagoon along the east edge: 7-cell strip full height plus a 5 x 15 bacino bulge at the canal mouth; lagoonEdge exported so the renderer draws that border as a breakwater
decisions.rationale: 'Open water along one edge'; 96 m of open water at the mouth is where big fights go; physics keeps the B ring
decisions.alternatives: Lagoon along the south edge under the hairpin (makes the quiet SW the hot zone and separates the covered bridge from the open water)

decisions.decision: Eight 1-wide side-canal networks; each links two thick-water places except three dead-end spurs; validator refuses any 2-wide water outside main canal and lagoon
decisions.rationale: 'One gondola fits easily, two scrape'; loops let hunters circle, nobody is forced to U-turn in 8 m; at most 4 dead ends so fleeing boats are not cornered
decisions.alternatives: 2-cell rii (16 m, ambush feel gone); more dead ends (too many traps)

decisions.decision: Walls as a greedy rectangle merge of B and T (69 rectangles for 1082 cells); piles as separate ball colliders; tower exported separately for the renderer
decisions.rationale: 69 cuboids instead of 1082 keeps the broad phase trivial and gives the art track 69 blocks; merging T is correct for physics
decisions.alternatives: Per-cell colliders (1082, visible seams); a trimesh of the water outline (hollow in Rapier, more code)

decisions.decision: Origin at the centre, row 0 = north = negative z, heading = Rapier rotation angle with forward (cos h, sin h) in (x, z), mesh.rotation.y = -heading
decisions.rationale: One rule for sim and renderer; proved by running Rapier (collider along local +x lands at (cos, sin)) and three (makeRotationY maps +x to (cos, 0, -sin))
decisions.alternatives: Row 0 at positive z (text upside down versus the top-down minimap)

decisions.decision: Dock heading = away from the quay: sum of (dock - B neighbour) vectors, best dot with an open direction, ties by water ahead then E,W,S,N
decisions.rationale: Boats spawn facing open water, dead-end docks face the exit; deterministic and covered by a test that the cell ahead is never a building
decisions.alternatives: Hand-written headings per dock (drift out of step with the text)

decisions.decision: parseMap throws MapError at import time for structural breakage; design checks (counts, widths, diameter, density, Monte Carlo) live in shared/map.test.ts; validate.mjs is the standalone design tool
decisions.rationale: A broken edit fails npm run dev and npm test in a second; the heavy checks cost ~100 ms, too much for import
decisions.alternatives: Only a test (a bad merge could reach the demo PC); everything at import (slow startup)

decisions.decision: Accept a 616 m network diameter and 512 m main-canal length while the quickest west-to-lagoon crossing is 360 m
decisions.rationale: 616 m equals the Manhattan distance between the grid's opposite corners (47 + 30 cells), so no shorter water network exists at this size; the spec's 'roughly 40 s' matches the 36 s shortcut via rio N2
decisions.alternatives: Shrinking the map or removing the far corners (loses the quiet respawn pockets the 80 m rule needs)

toolu_01NbhQaavQ9RWan9bcQe6Use.summary: Designed a 50 x 38 cell (400 x 304 m, 8 m cells) Venice district that satisfies SPEC.md section 7 and the respawn/crate/minimap rules, and proved it with an executable validator. The main canal is a reversed S like the Canal Grande: 4 cells (32 m) wide on the straights, a 45-degree run painted 5 cells tall so every cell is inside a 3x3 water window (24 m minimum), entering at the west edge, hairpin at col 13, exiting east under a 2x4 covered bridge (new legend char R, water for physics) into a 7-cell lagoon strip plus a 5x15 bacino bulge (new legend char P for pile clusters as 2.5 m balls). Eight 1-wide side-canal networks (215 cells, 1.7 km, 31 tight bends, 19 mouths, 3 dead ends), 7 arch bridges (3 over the main canal) + 1 covered, tower 52 m from the centre on a water-edge wedge, 16 docks (every quadrant, never adjacent, each with a quay; Monte Carlo 100% of 4000 random 5-enemy layouts leave a dock >= 80 m away, mean 7.3 candidates), 24 crates (12 in the lagoon, densest 40 m cluster of 7 in the bacino, farthest crate 136 m by water from a dock). Network diameter 77 cells = 616 m (62 s at 10 m/s), which equals the Manhattan distance of the grid's opposite corners, so it cannot be shorter; the quickest west-to-lagoon crossing is 360 m = 36 s via rio N2 (the spec's "roughly 40 s"). Deliverables in the scratch folder: map.txt (38 lines of 50 chars), validate.mjs (standalone, prints ALL CHECKS PASSED), gen.mjs (painter), annotate.mjs, final.md (94 KB, with the map, annotated rendering, validator output, decisions, algorithms, edge cases, day-one tests, sources), and TypeScript ready to paste: ts/shared/map.ts (parser: Legend type, parseMap -> {width,height,cells,navigable,lagoon,lagoonEdge,lagoonCells,walls(greedy merged rects, 69 for 1082 solid cells),docks{x,z,heading},crates,bridges{x,z,orientation,length,width,kind},tower,piles}, cellAt/colOf/rowOf/cellCentre/isLagoon/isNavigable, MAP_TEXT, MAP), ts/shared/map.test.ts (vitest, 12 tests pass in 205 ms), ts/src/sim/mapPhysics.ts (Rapier cuboid/ball colliders, respawnCandidates) and ts/src/render/mapGeometry.ts (instanced placeholder district). All four TS files typecheck with the repo's exact tsconfig options plus noUnusedLocals/noUnusedParameters. Coordinates: origin at the centre, x = (col - W/2 + 0.5)*8, z = (row - H/2 + 0.5)*8, Y up, row 0 = north = negative z; heading = Rapier rotation angle (0 = +x, +PI/2 = +z), mesh.rotation.y = -heading, both proved by running the installed Rapier 0.21.0 and three 0.186.1. No file in the repo was created or modified.

decisions.decision: Grid 50 x 38 cells at 8 m with a full B border ring; parser is size-agnostic (>= 8 x 8)
decisions.rationale: Exactly the spec's 'about 50 x 38, 400 x 300 m'; the border ring is the physics box for free
decisions.alternatives: A separate world-bounds collider kept in step with the grid by hand

decisions.decision: Extend the legend with R (covered bridge, 2 cells deep x 4 across, water for physics) and P (pile cluster, solid ball of radius 2.5 m)
decisions.rationale: The spec needs a Rialto-style landmark and lagoon piles but gives no chars; R lets the renderer roof it, P is a cluster boats can slip around
decisions.alternatives: Encode the Rialto as '=' (renderer cannot tell it apart); a full 8 x 8 m solid P cell (a block, not poles)

decisions.decision: Main canal as a reversed S: west mouth rows 6-9, bend at col 29, 45-degree run painted 5 cells tall per column, hairpin at col 13, lower arm rows 23-26 into the bacino
decisions.rationale: 32 m on the straights, never under 24 m on the diagonal (every cell inside a 3x3 water window); the real Canal Grande is 30-90 m and is itself a reversed S; two blind corners on the lane
decisions.alternatives: 90-degree stair bends (inside corner cuts to 24 m, reads as stairs); a north-south lane (the lagoon side would then be short)

decisions.decision: Lagoon along the east edge: 7-cell strip full height plus a 5 x 15 bacino bulge at the canal mouth; lagoonEdge exported so the renderer draws that border as a breakwater
decisions.rationale: 'Open water along one edge'; 96 m of open water at the mouth is where big fights go; physics keeps the B ring
decisions.alternatives: Lagoon along the south edge under the hairpin (makes the quiet SW the hot zone and separates the covered bridge from the open water)

decisions.decision: Eight 1-wide side-canal networks; each links two thick-water places except three dead-end spurs; validator refuses any 2-wide water outside main canal and lagoon
decisions.rationale: 'One gondola fits easily, two scrape'; loops let hunters circle, nobody is forced to U-turn in 8 m; at most 4 dead ends so fleeing boats are not cornered
decisions.alternatives: 2-cell rii (16 m, ambush feel gone); more dead ends (too many traps)

decisions.decision: Walls as a greedy rectangle merge of B and T (69 rectangles for 1082 cells); piles as separate ball colliders; tower exported separately for the renderer
decisions.rationale: 69 cuboids instead of 1082 keeps the broad phase trivial and gives the art track 69 blocks; merging T is correct for physics
decisions.alternatives: Per-cell colliders (1082, visible seams); a trimesh of the water outline (hollow in Rapier, more code)

decisions.decision: Origin at the centre, row 0 = north = negative z, heading = Rapier rotation angle with forward (cos h, sin h) in (x, z), mesh.rotation.y = -heading
decisions.rationale: One rule for sim and renderer; proved by running Rapier (collider along local +x lands at (cos, sin)) and three (makeRotationY maps +x to (cos, 0, -sin))
decisions.alternatives: Row 0 at positive z (text upside down versus the top-down minimap)

decisions.decision: Dock heading = away from the quay: sum of (dock - B neighbour) vectors, best dot with an open direction, ties by water ahead then E,W,S,N
decisions.rationale: Boats spawn facing open water, dead-end docks face the exit; deterministic and covered by a test that the cell ahead is never a building
decisions.alternatives: Hand-written headings per dock (drift out of step with the text)

decisions.decision: parseMap throws MapError at import time for structural breakage; design checks (counts, widths, diameter, density, Monte Carlo) live in shared/map.test.ts; validate.mjs is the standalone design tool
decisions.rationale: A broken edit fails npm run dev and npm test in a second; the heavy checks cost ~100 ms, too much for import
decisions.alternatives: Only a test (a bad merge could reach the demo PC); everything at import (slow startup)

decisions.decision: Accept a 616 m network diameter and 512 m main-canal length while the quickest west-to-lagoon crossing is 360 m
decisions.rationale: 616 m equals the Manhattan distance between the grid's opposite corners (47 + 30 cells), so no shorter water network exists at this size; the spec's 'roughly 40 s' matches the 36 s shortcut via rio N2
decisions.alternatives: Shrinking the map or removing the far corners (loses the quiet respawn pockets the 80 m rule needs)

data.topic: The Venice map for shared/map.ts: ASCII district, parser, coordinate rules, validation
data.summary: Designed a 50 x 38 cell (400 x 304 m, 8 m cells) Venice district that satisfies SPEC.md section 7 and the respawn/crate/minimap rules, and proved it with an executable validator. The main canal is a reversed S like the Canal Grande: 4 cells (32 m) wide on the straights, a 45-degree run painted 5 cells tall so every cell is inside a 3x3 water window (24 m minimum), entering at the west edge, hairpin at col 13, exiting east under a 2x4 covered bridge (new legend char R, water for physics) into a 7-cell lagoon strip plus a 5x15 bacino bulge (new legend char P for pile clusters as 2.5 m balls). Eight 1-wide side-canal networks (215 cells, 1.7 km, 31 tight bends, 19 mouths, 3 dead ends), 7 arch bridges (3 over the main canal) + 1 covered, tower 52 m from the centre on a water-edge wedge, 16 docks (every quadrant, never adjacent, each with a quay; Monte Carlo 100% of 4000 random 5-enemy layouts leave a dock >= 80 m away, mean 7.3 candidates), 24 crates (12 in the lagoon, densest 40 m cluster of 7 in the bacino, farthest crate 136 m by water from a dock). Network diameter 77 cells = 616 m (62 s at 10 m/s), which equals the Manhattan distance of the grid's opposite corners, so it cannot be shorter; the quickest west-to-lagoon crossing is 360 m = 36 s via rio N2 (the spec's "roughly 40 s"). Deliverables in the scratch folder: map.txt (38 lines of 50 chars), validate.mjs (standalone, prints ALL CHECKS PASSED), gen.mjs (painter), annotate.mjs, final.md (94 KB, with the map, annotated rendering, validator output, decisions, algorithms, edge cases, day-one tests, sources), and TypeScript ready to paste: ts/shared/map.ts (parser: Legend type, parseMap -> {width,height,cells,navigable,lagoon,lagoonEdge,lagoonCells,walls(greedy merged rects, 69 for 1082 solid cells),docks{x,z,heading},crates,bridges{x,z,orientation,length,width,kind},tower,piles}, cellAt/colOf/rowOf/cellCentre/isLagoon/isNavigable, MAP_TEXT, MAP), ts/shared/map.test.ts (vitest, 12 tests pass in 205 ms), ts/src/sim/mapPhysics.ts (Rapier cuboid/ball colliders, respawnCandidates) and ts/src/render/mapGeometry.ts (instanced placeholder district). All four TS files typecheck with the repo's exact tsconfig options plus noUnusedLocals/noUnusedParameters. Coordinates: origin at the centre, x = (col - W/2 + 0.5)*8, z = (row - H/2 + 0.5)*8, Y up, row 0 = north = negative z; heading = Rapier rotation angle (0 = +x, +PI/2 = +z), mesh.rotation.y = -heading, both proved by running the installed Rapier 0.21.0 and three 0.186.1. No file in the repo was created or modified.

decisions.decision: Grid 50 x 38 cells at 8 m with a full B border ring; parser is size-agnostic (>= 8 x 8)
decisions.rationale: Exactly the spec's 'about 50 x 38, 400 x 300 m'; the border ring is the physics box for free
decisions.alternatives: A separate world-bounds collider kept in step with the grid by hand

decisions.decision: Extend the legend with R (covered bridge, 2 cells deep x 4 across, water for physics) and P (pile cluster, solid ball of radius 2.5 m)
decisions.rationale: The spec needs a Rialto-style landmark and lagoon piles but gives no chars; R lets the renderer roof it, P is a cluster boats can slip around
decisions.alternatives: Encode the Rialto as '=' (renderer cannot tell it apart); a full 8 x 8 m solid P cell (a block, not poles)

decisions.decision: Main canal as a reversed S: west mouth rows 6-9, bend at col 29, 45-degree run painted 5 cells tall per column, hairpin at col 13, lower arm rows 23-26 into the bacino
decisions.rationale: 32 m on the straights, never under 24 m on the diagonal (every cell inside a 3x3 water window); the real Canal Grande is 30-90 m and is itself a reversed S; two blind corners on the lane
decisions.alternatives: 90-degree stair bends (inside corner cuts to 24 m, reads as stairs); a north-south lane (the lagoon side would then be short)

decisions.decision: Lagoon along the east edge: 7-cell strip full height plus a 5 x 15 bacino bulge at the canal mouth; lagoonEdge exported so the renderer draws that border as a breakwater
decisions.rationale: 'Open water along one edge'; 96 m of open water at the mouth is where big fights go; physics keeps the B ring
decisions.alternatives: Lagoon along the south edge under the hairpin (makes the quiet SW the hot zone and separates the covered bridge from the open water)

decisions.decision: Eight 1-wide side-canal networks; each links two thick-water places except three dead-end spurs; validator refuses any 2-wide water outside main canal and lagoon
decisions.rationale: 'One gondola fits easily, two scrape'; loops let hunters circle, nobody is forced to U-turn in 8 m; at most 4 dead ends so fleeing boats are not cornered
decisions.alternatives: 2-cell rii (16 m, ambush feel gone); more dead ends (too many traps)

decisions.decision: Walls as a greedy rectangle merge of B and T (69 rectangles for 1082 cells); piles as separate ball colliders; tower exported separately for the renderer
decisions.rationale: 69 cuboids instead of 1082 keeps the broad phase trivial and gives the art track 69 blocks; merging T is correct for physics
decisions.alternatives: Per-cell colliders (1082, visible seams); a trimesh of the water outline (hollow in Rapier, more code)

decisions.decision: Origin at the centre, row 0 = north = negative z, heading = Rapier rotation angle with forward (cos h, sin h) in (x, z), mesh.rotation.y = -heading
decisions.rationale: One rule for sim and renderer; proved by running Rapier (collider along local +x lands at (cos, sin)) and three (makeRotationY maps +x to (cos, 0, -sin))
decisions.alternatives: Row 0 at positive z (text upside down versus the top-down minimap)

decisions.decision: Dock heading = away from the quay: sum of (dock - B neighbour) vectors, best dot with an open direction, ties by water ahead then E,W,S,N
decisions.rationale: Boats spawn facing open water, dead-end docks face the exit; deterministic and covered by a test that the cell ahead is never a building
decisions.alternatives: Hand-written headings per dock (drift out of step with the text)

decisions.decision: parseMap throws MapError at import time for structural breakage; design checks (counts, widths, diameter, density, Monte Carlo) live in shared/map.test.ts; validate.mjs is the standalone design tool
decisions.rationale: A broken edit fails npm run dev and npm test in a second; the heavy checks cost ~100 ms, too much for import
decisions.alternatives: Only a test (a bad merge could reach the demo PC); everything at import (slow startup)

decisions.decision: Accept a 616 m network diameter and 512 m main-canal length while the quickest west-to-lagoon crossing is 360 m
decisions.rationale: 616 m equals the Manhattan distance between the grid's opposite corners (47 + 30 cells), so no shorter water network exists at this size; the spec's 'roughly 40 s' matches the 36 s shortcut via rio N2
decisions.alternatives: Shrinking the map or removing the far corners (loses the quiet respawn pockets the 80 m rule needs)

open_questions: The spec says 'crossable in roughly 40 s'; the shortest west-to-lagoon crossing is 36 s but the network diameter is 62 s and the main canal alone is 51 s. If the team wants the far corners closer, the only lever at 50 x 38 is to shrink the lagoon strip or the SW quarter; decide at the Gate 2 playtest.

Side-canal 'count': the spec's 'about 8' is matched by 8 connected one-wide networks, but one of them (W3+S1+S4) is a 95-cell ring. If the team wants 8 separate rii, break the S4-to-S1 link at (14,33) with a B (adds a dead end, total 4).
Whether a dock adjacent to the bacino (36,23) should count as 'in the lagoon' for the minimap reveal; the lagoon mask currently includes it. Easy to change by excluding S from LAGOON_PASS.
Bridge clearance (4 m above water) and the covered bridge roof height are placeholders for track C; the physics does not care.

Crate drift: crates are light bodies in the spec; the sim should clamp a crate back toward its cell centre when it drifts more than ~4 m so it never ends up against an abutment under a bridge. Not implemented here (sim topic).
